nodes.body: Audited against merged main c193451587f6e84116ae1f4714b5a37446dc7053. The native cell intentionally admits only identity perspective divide (w == 1) with x/y in [-1, 1] and z in [0, 1]; another stream returns the initialization failure that the queue maps to device loss. Full arbitrary homogeneous perspective division and clipping needs a separate vertex execution design and independent calibration, outside this bounded arming fix. No hardware claim is made, so this residual remains unresolved.

Merged main retains an explicit bounded carrier contract: r3v_native_cell.c rejects non-unit w and vertices outside the admitted NDC volume, while the public harness calibrates in-domain vertices plus w=2 and NaN refusal. The current three-vertex carrier and fixed IB cannot implement Vulkan homogeneous clipping, generated primitive topology, interpolation, and viewport mapping without a separate mechanism. The host/drm-shim surface passes r3v-native-public-surface, r3v-native-vertex-carrier, r3v-native-triangle-cell-closed, and r3v-native-triangle-cell-open (4/4); this is not hardware or runtime evidence. The thread stays unresolved. A future fix requires perspective division, all relevant clip-plane crossings, clipped-output representation, and calibrated proof that valid non-unit-w streams no longer become device loss.

The current merged tree still rejects arbitrary homogeneous positions at this cell; it does not yet own a native clip-space representation, six-plane clipping, finite-W handling, interpolation, or fan triangulation. No clipper implementation or RS482 runtime witness exists, so the VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST path remains an evidence-bound open item. I leave this thread unresolved until a complete native clipper and its focused tests are present.
